idiom_name: kotlinx.coroutines with Dispatchers.IO for the blocking layer and a Channel as the queue
implementation_notes: The asynchronous layer is the coroutine dispatcher machinery; blocking calls are moved to Dispatchers.IO (or a dedicated limited-parallelism dispatcher) so they never occupy the CPU dispatcher, and the queueing layer is a kotlinx.coroutines Channel or Flow. The boundary primitives are withContext(Dispatchers.IO) to run blocking code from a coroutine and runBlocking to enter the coroutine world from synchronous code. Keep the classic pool-and-queue shape when the blocking work owns a bounded resource - a JDBC connection pool - that must be sized and monitored separately from CPU work.
pitfalls: Calling blocking APIs on Dispatchers.Default starves the CPU dispatcher; that hand-off is what Dispatchers.IO exists for.
Dispatchers.IO is a shared, elastic pool unless limitedParallelism is used, so one component's blocking storm can delay unrelated work.
runBlocking inside a coroutine deadlocks the dispatcher it runs on; keep it at the outermost boundary (main, tests, legacy callers).
Cancelling the consuming coroutine does not interrupt a blocking call already running in Dispatchers.IO; cooperatively check cancellation between jobs.
